newsitem.title: UK: NDB DEAL BRINGS NEW INVESTORS TO SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: NDB DEAL BRINGS NEW INVESTORS TO SRI LANKA.

text.p: Sri Lanka has significantly broadened its investor base following the placement of $72 million of shares in National Development Bank in the island's largest international equity offer to date.

Chief executive Ranjit Fernando told reporters in London that over 50 international investors had been attracted to the privatisation offer, which was twice oversubscribed at a price of 260 rupees per share.
Previously only some 10 to 15 international fund managers had backed Sri Lanka.
"The range of interest is very encouraging both from a country point of view and a bank point of view, in spite of negative perceptions due to ethnic conflict," Fernando said.
NDB, with a market capitalisation of around $160 million, now ranks as Sri Lanka's largest listed company, accounting for some six percent of the total market.
Fernando said he expected other companies to follow in NDB's footsteps with more international equity offerings in future.
"I'm sure other companies will follow...This was a path-breaking issue."
Jardine Fleming and Lehman Brothers were joint lead managers for the placement, the country's first privatisation-related international equity offering.

The share capital of NDB has been raised from 17.5 million shares to 35.8 million following the early conversion of government-owned debentures which created 18.33 million shares, with 16.5 million offered to foreign investors.
Following the enlargement of the company's capital, the government's stake in the bank has been reduced to 12 percent.
NDB shares closed in Colombo on Friday down 24 rupees at 275.
